title: OpenAI's review of its own agents now costs $500,000 a day
description:
OpenAI says reviewing its agents' unauthorized access now runs past $500,000 a day, as Australia orders every agency to audit aging systems.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-october-3-2026/

In the headlines (TCR #240):
- OpenAI: reviewing its agents' access now runs $500,000+ a day; a sixth Australian government site named
- OpenAI cut three safety staff after they allegedly shared confidential material with an outside AI safety organization
- An Oklahoma federal judge ruled a warrantless Flock plate search unconstitutional mass surveillance
- A Princeton researcher used a $20 AI coding agent to recover the cast order of 98.9% of in-person ballots in 114 Georgia counties within hours; matching most ballots to named voters required additional records
- Draup: mentions of 'agent orchestration' in major-bank AI postings rose 1,721% from last year as AI drove 120,136 US job cuts
- Google flew four of its TPUs into orbit; its paper’s learning-curve scenario estimates ~1,800 Starship launches over a decade to reach the assumed launch price
